newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania government wants end to state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Albania government wants end to state of emergency.

text.p: Albania's nine-party national unity government has asked President Sali Berisha to end a state of emergency to allow parties to campaign normally for forthcoming elections, a government spokesman said on Sunday.
The edict was slapped on the country on March 2 as riots and looting spilled over into an uprising against Berisha. It includes a nationwide curfew from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.

"The government decided to propose to the president the lifting of the state of emergency as the election day has been set in order to create the most proper conditions for parties," a government spokesman told Reuters.
He said it was up to the president to decree the lifting of the emergency, as parliament was dissolved earlier this month after the June 29 election day was named.

Albania, Europe's poorest nation, vitally needs the election to restore law and order after anger over the collapse of get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes spilled over into a rebellion against Berisha.
Although the situation has calmed, large swathes of the country remain outside government control and it is saturated with more than a million weapons looted during the troubles in private hands.
